title: Animation iteration, direction, fill, play state
learningObjectives: Explain animation iteration, direction, fill, play state and apply the concept in maintainable CSS.

understand.concept: CSS animation controls include iteration-count, direction, fill-mode, and play-state. These determine how many times an animation runs, whether it reverses, which keyframe styles apply before or after the active interval, and whether it is paused or running.
understand.whyItMatters: Animation timing and persistence affect user experience. Infinite movement can distract; fill modes can leave an element in a visually altered state after the animation. Use finite, intentional motion and reduced-motion support.
understand.analogy: An animation has a route, a direction, a number of trips, and a pause control.
understand.analogyLimit: The analogy simplifies the idea; actual cascade, inheritance, and rendering follow CSS specifications.

explain.narrative: The element moves back and forth for two iterations. Change alternate to normal and both to forwards to compare.

examples.explanation: The element moves back and forth for two iterations. Change alternate to normal and both to forwards to compare.
examples.expectedOutput: A rendered example showing the relevant CSS behaviour.

practise.guidedTask: Create a finite animation that runs twice, reverses direction, and retains the final keyframe style. Explain each animation control.
practise.independentTask: Build a small component or page section that uses the concept. Test alternate content and, where relevant, right-to-left direction or reduced-motion settings.
hints: Inspect computed styles and inherited values.
Change one declaration at a time.
Keep user preferences and writing direction in mind.

questions.prompt: Which property pauses or resumes a CSS animation?
What is a maintainable way to use CSS features across a project?
options: Use clear reusable rules and test computed behaviour
Copy unrelated declarations into every component
Ignore writing direction and user preferences
questions.answer: Use clear reusable rules and test computed behaviour
questions.explanation: Reusable CSS should remain understandable and work across relevant content and user settings.
